processing: Little is documented in detail. Listed here as black tea, made as usual for estate black tea by withering, rolling, oxidising and drying.
harvest_season: Little is documented about seasons here. At this latitude, tea is generally picked through much of the year rather than in one short spring harvest.
appearance_dry: Dark, as usual for estate black tea; grades vary.
appearance_liquor: Reddish amber, typical of black tea.
taste_profile: Few tasting records exist. Expect what is typical of estate black tea: brisk and malty, suited to a plain strong cup.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western-style, like other estate black tea. Takes milk or sugar well if it comes out strong.

vintage_note: Sold in Indonesia as an everyday packaged brand, at modest prices and with no vintage. As with other everyday black tea, buy it fresh and check the best-before date.
description:
Kayu Aro is a large tea plantation in Kerinci, in the Jambi highlands of Sumatra, above 1,400 metres. The same name appears on packets in Indonesian shops, so it means both a place and an everyday brand.

Details of its current making are thin on the ground. Treat it as estate black tea of the kind typical of the region, and judge what you buy on its own merits.

In the cup, expect a brisk, plain and fairly strong tea. That is what is usual for the class, since few independent tasting notes exist. A normal Western steep suits it.

It is cheap and easy to find in Indonesia, and worth bringing home as a taste of the place. It isn't a connoisseur's collectable, and it isn't sold as one.
history:
The Dutch firm NV HVA (Handels Vereeniging Amsterdam) developed Kayu Aro from about 1925. Javanese workers were brought to the district as contract labourers in the colonial period, and the plantation shaped the local community.

Today it is run by PTPN IV PalmCo.
